title: @throws {Never} is a declared channel that names no resolvable Error class, not the trusted opt-out
notes: specification/failures.mdx:115 (Locked): '`@throws {never}` removes the default panic case; `@throws {T}` declares the stated foreign error channel.' The spelling the sentence prints is lowercase, and `Never` is therefore the second form, not the first: a declared channel whose Error constructor has to be resolvable. No class named `Never` is in scope in conformance/support/capitalized-never.ts, so the declaration cannot be reified (SMITHERS1502) and the call keeps its panic policy, leaving an unconsumed Result (SMITHERS1301). A case-insensitive comparison turns the same source into the trusted opt-out with no diagnostic at all, which is the fail-open direction: `probe` would be certified infallible. The lowercase spelling is pinned by 09-foreign-calls/trusted-foreign-call-is-accepted, whose `double` is annotated `@throws {never}` and needs no Result channel, so the pair fixes the case rule from both sides. Both diagnostics are declared because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract (conformance/README.md); they share an authored position because both belong to the same call.
